paragraphs: Friend, the believers in this passage got scattered, and they did NOT stop talking. They went where they were pushed and preached the word wherever they went (Acts 8:4). I know what it's like to get moved somewhere you didn't pick, and the lesson here is that a bad landing spot can still be a good place to share Jesus.

Then there's Simon. He had a whole city saying, "This man is the divine power called the Great Power" (Acts 8:10), and still he looked at the Holy Spirit and saw something he could buy. Peter told him, "you thought you could buy the gift of God with money!" (Acts 8:20). Friend, God's gifts aren't for sale, and no amount of silver or reputation gets you a seat at His table. I think that's the hardest part of this story to hear, and it's meant to be.

But look at what Peter does next. He doesn't slam the door. He says, "Repent, therefore, of your wickedness, and pray to the Lord. Perhaps He will forgive you for the intent of your heart" (Acts 8:22). So guard your heart, baker, and when it's off, run back to the Lord instead of trying to cover it up. And keep your ovens warm like Peter and John did, because they headed home preaching the gospel in many Samaritan villages (Acts 8:25).
